snippet.title: The Future of Creativity Is #NotGenerated | An Adobe × Parsons Collaboration
snippet.description:
A Parsons student downloaded 70,000 lines of her own data, fed it to AI, and asked what it knew about her. The answer described her with unsettling accuracy. 

That's where Not Generated starts — with what it means for the people learning to create alongside AI. To explore this topic further, and what creativity means in the age of AI, students, faculty, and industry voices gathered for a symposium, a hands-on Creative AI Lab and a final exhibition at @thenewschool.

AI is moving faster than the questions around it. Who gets credit? What's ethical? What does it mean to make something? In a partnership between Adobe and The New School, we asked students and faculty to sit with those questions. 

Like Julienne DeVita, adjunct professor at Parsons, said: "The future of creativity is not generated; it needs to be consciously shaped through critical collaboration between humans and artificial partners." 

____

snippet.title: Cracking the Semaphore Code | Adobe
snippet.description:
After three years, the San Jose Semaphore has been solved! The puzzle, created by Ben Rubin, features rotating discs at the top of Adobe’s Almaden Tower that hide a secret message through data points of bytes and numbered colors.  

When creating the puzzle, Ben sprinkled in footholds for the code breaker to latch onto when starting to assess it. He also balanced it with red herrings to make the puzzle interesting to solve with the right amount of redundant information. 

The difficulty level? Perfect. At least, that’s what Brian Vincent said after solving the puzzle. As a software engineer, Brian understood data and recognized patterns in what the Semaphore was communicating. However, it took stepping away from the puzzle for about a year for him to feel like he was making progress.  

“In some ways it seems a little bit simple, but at the same time it takes a lot of work and a lot of effort, and it stands for years before anyone solves it,” said Brian.  

Will you attempt to solve the next iteration of the San Jose Semaphore?

snippet.title: Made to Create | Scott Hansen is Tycho | Adobe
snippet.description:
Scott Hansen always loved music, but never imagined he could be the one creating it. And while he dreamed of making art, he struggled to translate the ideas in his head until he discovered Photoshop in 1995.  

Known as the artist @Tychomusic, he was introduced to electronic music as a college student and felt a real connection to it. Fast-forward to today, Scott's creating chillwave and ambient electronic music, pairing it with album-related art and tour prints, all made using Adobe tools. 

“Adobe, as a concept, their tools have been the cornerstone of my creative process for about 30 years now. It’s the first thing I learned on, and it’s all I’ve ever used.”  
 
Tycho is Made to Create, and he’s spent his career finding ways to overcome impediments to get his vision out into the world — both musically and visually.  

Adobe tools are a key part of his workflow, allowing him to create and share his art with the world.

snippet.title: Be You: Why Having a Point of View as a Staff Product Designer is Important | Adobe Life
snippet.description:
Meet Em Siegel, Staff Product Designer at Adobe. 

Outside of work, Em is a ceramicist. Throwing pots satisfies a tactile need their screen-based work can't, but the two practices aren't as separate as it may seem. When Em considers how a piece will feel in someone's hands, they're thinking through the same user experience questions they bring to designing features in Adobe tools. 

“Authenticity really goes a long way.”  

Discover how having a point of view, creativity, and career development come together in a career at Adobe. Learn more: https://adobe.ly/4dnWqKZ

snippet.title: The Coolest Job: Come Work with Navin Watumull
snippet.description:

snippet.description:

Whether you’re just starting or refining your approach, this session offers practical takeaways and fresh inspiration.

• Why owning your audience is essential
• How to balance experimentation with consistency
• Monetization streams that work
• Choosing a niche and unique voice
• The parasocial bond’s role in trust
• Why quantity is better than quality early on
• The realities of making content a career

snippet.title: Be You: From Barista to Business Development Representative at Adobe | Adobe Life
snippet.description:
What’s it like to grow your career at Adobe? For Amanda Valenzuela, it started with a conversation. 

As a Business Development Representative, Amanda works with marketing leaders to support growth using Adobe Marketo, Adobe Analytics, and Adobe Journey Optimizer. Her journey at Adobe began as a barista at our San Jose HQ, where she built relationships, shared her career goals, and found leaders who believed in her potential. 

Outside of work, Amanda is an illustrator, muralist, potter, and sticker artist. Inside Adobe, she’s part of a creative employee community where different backgrounds, roles, and passions are valued. 

Discover how Amanda’s creativity, connection, and ambition shaped her career path and how Adobe supports employees in growing new opportunities.

snippet.title: Super Session: Future-Proofing Your Design Career in the Age of AI | Adobe
snippet.description:
Learn how to stay relevant and thrive as the design world evolves. Explore what makes us valuable as designers when AI tools change how we work. Drawing on insights from Samantha Warren, Senior Director of Design, Adobe Firefly, and designer, performer, and educator Meg Lewis, we'll examine the shift from purely technical skills to the uniquely human qualities that AI cannot replicate, providing practical strategies for cultivating your most valuable asset as a designer — your humanity. The session will wrap with an inspiring demo by Adobe designers Brooke Hopper and Danielle Morimoto that reveals how Firefly enhances the flow of ideas and supports the creative process.

You will:


• Discover techniques to strengthen your storytelling abilities and create unexpected design solutions beyond what AI can produce
• Learn approaches to deepen your empathy and connection-building skills to solve more complex design challenges
• Gain insights on evolving your role beyond pixel creation toward design leadership, integrating human context and vision
• Identify ways to capitalize on your unique non-design experiences and passions as competitive advantages in an AI-augmented industry

snippet.title: The Heart and Mind of Editing Award-Winning Music Videos | Adobe
snippet.description:
Editing isn’t just technical — it’s emotional, psychological, and deeply human. In this session, editor Vinnie Hobbs, of VH Post and Union Editorial, shares the mindset that’s helped him cut award-winning music videos and commercials, not just with skill, but with soul. You’ll explore what it means to edit with intention, how to stay inspired when burnout hits, and why stepping out from behind the screen is just as vital as mastering it.

This talk isn’t a software tutorial — it’s about purpose, passion, and the long game. Join Vinnie as he shares thoughts and inspiration on:

• How to reignite your creative spark when the work feels draining
• Understanding how personal growth fuels editorial growth
• Why networking and confidence matter as much as technique
• Redefining “success” as an editor beyond the timeline
• How to build a career, not just a reel

snippet.title: Building your Brand Image across Social Media using MOGRTs | Adobe
snippet.description:
In today’s scroll-heavy world, consistent branding across your videos is key to standing out. In this session, content creator Josh Olufemii shows how to build a strong, unified visual identity using Motion Graphics Templates (MOGRTs) in Premiere Pro. You’ll learn how to create a personal color palette and customize and deploy MOGRTs across platforms like YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok to create a cohesive brand look. No After Effects expertise required!

In this practical and fast-paced session, you’ll learn how to:

• Build a personal brand look using MOGRTs inside Premiere Pro
• Customize templates to match your visual identity
• Elevate your brand without needing to touch After Effects

snippet.title: Scrappy, Smart, and Human: The Future of Storytelling | Adobe
snippet.description:
• In an age of algorithm-chasing headlines and shrinking attention spans, Emmy-winning filmmaker and journalist Johnny Harris invites you inside the storytelling ethos that drives his work — one that prioritizes curiosity over clicks and stories over soundbites. Drawing on experience with Vox and The New York Times, Johnny shows how storytelling isn’t just about what you say but how you invite others to care. Known for his scrappy, visual-first approach, he breaks down the ingredients of compelling narratives and the tools he uses to make them resonate.

What You’ll Learn:

• How to spark curiosity instead of chasing clicks
• Key ingredients of memorable, compelling stories
• A visual-first approach to storytelling that connects
• Practical tools and techniques for creating impactful narratives

snippet.title: Better Together: Illustrator + InDesign for Editorial Design | Adobe
snippet.description:
When using InDesign, we often rely on basic geometric image frames such as squares, circles, and rectangles to add visual interest. But what if your designs could break free from those boundaries? Imagine using parametric patterns, expressive word art, paper cutouts, or organic shapes that break through the frame and flow onto the page. In this session, Sam Luo from LYH Studio shows you how to elevate your editorial layouts — like books, magazines, newspapers, and lookbooks — by pairing the creative flexibility of Illustrator with the layout power of InDesign. Ditch the cookie-cutter look and start designing layouts that truly stand out.

You’ll learn:

• A proven workflow to design complex vector graphics in Illustrator and bring them seamlessly into InDesign
• Best practices for linking, scaling, and managing Illustrator assets inside InDesign
• When and how to use this workflow to enhance visual storytelling

snippet.description:

🔹 Explored bias in AI systems and inclusive persona design

snippet.title: How You Made It, Ep. 1 | Art, Authorship, and the Power of Being Seen | Adobe Content Authenticity
snippet.description:
What happens when your work travels around the Internet, gets shared by millions of people, but your involvement gets lost along the way?

Lack of attribution or credit is an all too familiar story for many artists and often result in lost opportunity. In this episode of How You Made It, illustrator Fabiola Lara and photographer Aundre Larrow reunite from their days at the college newspaper to talk about art, authorship, and how the free Adobe Content Authenticity web app is helping artists protect their work and reclaim their presence online.

Watch or listen to this first episode of How You Made It by Adobe Content Authenticity to explore:
- What it really means to “make it” as a modern artist
- Why creative attribution matters more than ever in the age of generative AI
- How to apply and customize your Content Credentials with the free web app

snippet.title: How Nature Inspires Creativity at Adobe Create Camp | Adobe
snippet.description:
What happens when you step away from the studio and into the outdoors? We’re discovering how the shapes, colors, and rhythms of nature can spark entirely new ways of thinking and creating together.

We invite you to step outside, slow down, and really observe. Because when you let the world around you guide your imagination, the best ideas have room to grow—often far beyond the lines. 🌳
